Save a pedigree diagram as a picture file

Source: R/savePedigreeDiagram.R
savePedigreeDiagram.Rd

Writes the widget drawPedigreeDiagram returns as a picture file, from a script: it is drawn in a browser by JavaScript, and nothing else in R can turn it into a file. A headless Chrome (through the chromote package) runs the very drawing the widget shows, a small recording layer writes every line, shape and word it draws, and the result is an SVG file: the same drawing, with every mark, colour and legend row, and each id as text that a reader can select, search and zoom to.

Usage

savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, file, width = NULL, height = NULL, dpi = 300)

Arguments

diagram

the widget drawPedigreeDiagram returns.

file

the file to write, one file name. Its ending, in any case, chooses the kind of file: .svg, .pdf or .png. The folder must exist.

width, height

the page, in inches: a positive number, or NULL (the default) for the size the widget has in the browser, 10 inches wide. The widget is drawn at width * 96 by height * 96 pixels, so the drawing fills the page, with its legend at the right.

dpi

the pixels per inch of the page in a .png file, one positive number (the default is 300): a page of 7 by 5 inches is 2100 by 1500 pixels. An .svg or .pdf file is vector and has no pixels, so the number does not change it; it is checked for every kind of file.

Value

file, invisibly.

Details

The ending of file chooses the kind of file: .svg, the recorded drawing as it is; .pdf, that drawing printed as one page of the picture's size, still vector, with each id as text (each dashed line is written as a row of short strokes, because Chrome writes every dash of a dashed line as an outline and a pedigree with many repeat animals would otherwise be a PDF of several megabytes); or .png, a photograph of the same drawing at dpi pixels per inch of the page.

The widget on screen draws an id only when it would be 4 pixels tall, so a large pedigree shows no ids until a reader zooms in. A file has no zoom, so the function writes every id: it lowers that limit on a copy of the widget, and the widget diagram itself is not changed.

The picture is the widget's size in the browser, 10 inches (960 pixels) wide, unless width or height say otherwise. The drawing and its legend are drawn for that page, and the file's own size is the page, so it prints at that size.

The function starts its own headless Chrome for each call (two for a .pdf or .png) and closes it, and stops if the drawing is not done within 60 seconds (options(pedkindraw.saveTimeout = seconds) changes that).

Requirements

The chromote package, and Google Chrome or Chromium on the computer (set CHROMOTE_CHROME to its path if chromote cannot find it). Both are checked before anything is drawn. A .pdf or .png file also needs jsonlite, which chromote needs too.

See also

drawPedigreeDiagram for the widget, and makePedigreeMatingLayout for what it draws.

Examples

# It starts Chrome, so it runs when typed in R, and not in R CMD check.
if (interactive() &&
      requireNamespace("chromote", quietly = TRUE) &&
      !is.null(suppressMessages(chromote::find_chrome()))) {
  ped <- data.frame(
    id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
    sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A"),
    dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B"),
    sex = c("M", "F", "F", "M"),
    status = c("DECEASED", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE"),
    affected = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
  diagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped))
  for (kind in c(".svg", ".pdf", ".png")) {
    file <- tempfile(fileext = kind)
    savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, file, width = 7, height = 5)
    print(file.exists(file))
    unlink(file)
  }
}
